chunks: From him, from Muhammad ibn al-Fudayl, from Abu al-Subah al-Kinani, who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the male slave: how many women are permissible for him? He said: two women.
ai.seo_question: How many wives can a male slave have according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In this hadith from al-Ishtibār, Imam al-Sadiq (as) clarifies that a male slave (mamluk) is permitted to marry up to two women, a restriction derived from the general principle of justice and capacity found in Quran 4:3. This ruling distinguishes the slave's status from that of a free man, who is allowed up to four wives, reflecting the juristic consensus that the limitation for slaves is based on their ability to maintain equitable treatment. The narration highlights the practical application of marital laws within the specific socio-legal framework of early Islamic society.
